summary: Our interactive game lets players design, manage, and simulate a complete NASA space mission from concept to operation. Players balance mission objectives, spacecraft design, instruments, launch vehicles, budget, power, mass, communications, and orbital constraints. Every engineering decision and resource trade-off shapes mission success, turning abstract concepts into hands-on learning. Through engaging simulation and real-time feedback, students explore how complex systems interact and discover what it takes to launch a successful mission.
details: Our project is an interactive NASA space mission game that allows players to design, manage, and simulate a complete space mission from concept to operation, starting with choosing a mission objective such as exploring Mars, studying an asteroid, or observing Earth, then designing their spacecraft by selecting a structure, power source, propulsion system, communication system, and scientific instruments, with every choice affecting budget, mass, power, and volume, before choosing a launch vehicle and target orbit and then running a live simulation where players must respond to real-time challenges like power shortages, communication delays, instrument failures, and budget overruns, make critical engineering decisions, reallocate resources, and keep the mission on track to achieve the highest possible science return. The game benefits students by turning abstract trade-offs into hands-on learning, teaching systems thinking, problem-solving, resource management, and critical thinking, while making space science accessible, engaging, and fun even for those with no prior engineering background, and by giving instant feedback so players can learn from failure without real-world risk. Its intended impact is to inspire more students to pursue STEM, aerospace engineering, and space science, help them understand why real NASA missions are so complex and require teamwork, provide teachers with a classroom-friendly tool to teach physics, math, and engineering design, and spark curiosity about future missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. To develop the project, our team used Unity for the web interface and menus, Figma for UI design and prototyping, Blender for spacecraft models and visuals, and custom formulas and spreadsheets to calculate realistic mass, power, budget, and orbital constraints, with the game designed to run on standard laptops and PCs in a browser without special hardware. The project is creative because instead of using quizzes or videos, it puts players in the role of mission designers, uses random events and branching outcomes so no two playthroughs are the same, and combines storytelling, strategy, and science into a mission control experience that feels like working at NASA. Throughout development, our team carefully considered key factors including budget limits, mass and power constraints, communication distance and delay, orbital mechanics and launch windows, scientific value of instruments, risk and reliability of cheaper parts, and user experience, ensuring the game is both educational, realistic, and enjoyable for all players.
